title: Simple yet effective modifications to the operation of the Sediment Isolation Microplastic unit to avoid polyvinyl chloride (PVC) contamination
author: Nel, Krause, et al.

steps.title: Prepare spiked sediment sample
steps.instruction: Weigh 30 g of clean sediment into a container and spike with a total of 20 microplastic fragments: 10 polyethylene terephthalate (PET) fragments plus either 10 polyethylene (PE) or 10 polypropylene (PP) fragments; homogenise gently.

steps.title: Load sediment into SMI unit
steps.instruction: Place the spiked sediment into the Sediment Isolation Microplastic (SMI) unit; do not use the ball valve (leave it open or removed) as per the modified protocol.

steps.title: Settle and decant supernatant
steps.instruction: Allow the denser sediment particles to settle; then carefully decant the supernatant from the unit.

steps.title: Rinse upper chamber
steps.instruction: Remove the upper chamber of the SMI unit and rinse it thoroughly to recover any particles adhering to the chamber walls; discard the rinsate into the collected supernatant.

steps.title: Concentrate supernatant on mesh
steps.instruction: Pass the combined supernatant through a 63 µm stainless‑steel mesh, washing the retained material into clean petri dishes.

steps.title: Oven‑dry recovered particles
steps.instruction: Place the petri dishes in an oven set to 50 °C and dry for 24 h.

steps.title: Analyse recovered microplastics
steps.instruction: After drying, count and identify the recovered microplastic particles under a microscope or appropriate imaging system.

steps.title: Run negative blanks for QC
steps.instruction: Prepare a sediment‑free ZnCl₂ solution and process it as a blank using the same steps; run 15 blanks (one after every 10 samples or at least once per day) to confirm no PVC contamination.
